seo_title: All {count} Patient Conditions in Animal Hospital
meta_description: Match Animal Hospital patient diagnoses with the correct treatment supply, including Medicine, Herbs, syrups, and duplicate Maple Syrup requests.
intro_md: Patient Conditions turn each room diagnosis into a supply match. The right item saves the patient, while a guess can kill them and remove a hospital life, so this is one shift where confidence should arrive after reading.
description_md:
## Treating a diagnosed patient

Wait for the room display to show the condition, then collect the matching supply from the treatment stations outside the patient rooms. Use it on the diagnosed patient only after confirming the room and condition.

A wrong treatment kills the patient and costs the hospital a life. In a team, calling out the room number, condition, and supply helps stop two players from curing different problems with the same bottle.

## Memorizing the treatment families

Hydration pairs Dried Eyes with Eyedrops and Dehydration with IV Drops. Anti-Inflammatory pairs Bruises with a Medkit and Fever with Thermo.

Skin Remedies pairs Rashes with Ointment and Bleeding with Bandages. Ache Remedies is the easy one to reverse under pressure: Headache uses Medicine, while Stomach Ache uses Herbs.

Syrups pairs Low Sugar and Canadian with Maple Syrup, while Flu uses Cough Syrup. Low Sugar and Canadian remain separate diagnoses even though the treatment is shared.

## Handling shared and extra supply uses

A patient can show Low Sugar and Canadian together. The game may ask for Maple Syrup twice, so one completed checkmark does not always mean the second diagnosis has quietly forgiven you.

Some treatment supplies also have uses in surgery care, fire care, or anomaly interactions. Those extra uses do not change the standard diagnosis mapping, and Room 8 surgery prompts remain a separate treatment flow.
how_it_works_md: Correct treatment gives the supply matched to the diagnosis. Supply location explains where normal treatment items are found, while Wrong treatment risk and Extra use cover failure consequences and supported secondary uses.

description_json.Hydration: Eyedrops treat Dried Eyes, while IV Drops treat Dehydration. The names are similar enough to reward reading the diagnosis instead of grabbing the nearest liquid.
description_json.Anti-Inflammatory: Medkit treats Bruises and Thermo treats Fever. Thermo is the treatment item name used by the game, not merely a temperature check.
description_json.Skin Remedies: Ointment treats Rashes and Bandages treat Bleeding. Ointment also has a separate fire-care use, but the displayed diagnosis still controls normal patient treatment.
description_json.Ache Remedies: Medicine treats Headache and Herbs treat Stomach Ache. Keeping that exact split avoids the most tempting shelf swap during a busy shift.
description_json.Syrups: Maple Syrup treats both Low Sugar and Canadian, which can create a double request when both appear. Cough Syrup is reserved for Flu.

faq_json.q: Does Headache use Medicine or Herbs in Animal Hospital?
faq_json.a: Headache uses Medicine. Herbs are the correct treatment for Stomach Ache.

faq_json.q: What treats Stomach Ache in Animal Hospital?
faq_json.a: Use Herbs for Stomach Ache. Medicine belongs to the Headache diagnosis.

faq_json.q: Why can a patient need Maple Syrup twice?
faq_json.a: Low Sugar and Canadian are separate diagnoses that both use Maple Syrup. If a patient has both, the game can request a second bottle.

faq_json.q: What happens if I use the wrong treatment?
faq_json.a: The patient dies and the hospital loses a life. Confirm the displayed condition before using a supply.

faq_json.q: Where are treatment supplies in Animal Hospital?
faq_json.a: Normal treatment supplies are found at the treatment stations outside the patient rooms.

faq_json.q: Are Room 8 surgery prompts standard Patient Conditions?
faq_json.a: No. Room 8 surgery care can request some of the same supplies, but it is a separate treatment flow from the displayed standard diagnoses.

Wrong treatment kills the patient and costs the hospital a life, so Medicine belongs to Headache and Herbs belong to Stomach Ache. Low Sugar and Canadian both use Maple Syrup and can create a double request on the same patient.
